data.outcome_summary: This OECD country note summarizes results from the Survey of Adult Skills 2023 for Croatia, covering adults aged 16–65 assessed in 2022–23 across three domains: literacy, numeracy, and adaptive problem solving. The assessment is administered exclusively on digital tablets and reports proficiency on 500-point scales with proficiency levels derived from task success/failure; uncertainty is shown via 95% confidence intervals. Croatia’s mean performance is below the OECD average in all three domains (literacy 254, numeracy 254, adaptive problem solving 235). The note reports proficiency-level shares, including relatively high proportions at or below Level 1 (literacy 28%, numeracy 27%, adaptive problem solving 39%) and lower shares at Levels 4–5 (e.g., numeracy 6%). It also documents associations between numeracy proficiency and employment/labour-force participation and wages, and between numeracy and well-being/civic outcomes, including that these relationships persist after controlling for socio-demographic characteristics; however, no ML model training, PV-combining, or missing-data/weighting specifics are provided in the excerpt.
